desc:
Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray of nums in which the difference between the largest and the smallest element is at most limit.

nums = [5, 1, 3, 4, 2, 9], limit = 3
[1,3,4,2] has largest 4, smallest 1, difference 3 -> length 4
[5,1,3,4,2] would have difference 4, so it is not allowed
result = 4
hints: Any single element is a valid subarray, so the answer is at least 1. Checking all O(n<sup>2</sup>) subarrays with a running max and min is too slow for the largest inputs.
If a subarray is valid then every subarray inside it is valid too. That is what makes a two-pointer window work: when the window becomes invalid, only the left end needs to move right.
You need the max and min of the current window while both ends move. Keep a decreasing deque (max) and an increasing deque (min) of indices, and advance the left end while max - min > limit.
editorial: Grow the window one element at a time at the right end. Keep two monotonic deques of indices, one for the maximum (values decreasing) and one for the minimum (values increasing). While the difference between the two front values exceeds limit, move the left end l forward and drop deque fronts whose index is below l. The remaining window is the longest valid window ending at the current position; record its length.

The window never needs to move left again because a valid subarray stays valid when it shrinks, so the left pointer only increases. Each index is pushed and popped at most once in each deque: O(n) time and O(n) space in the worst case.
